title: 'Leon was apologising': How an illegal move cost Abhimanyu a sure-shot win in GCL
content: Abhimanyu Mishra’s winning position against Leon Luke Mendonca turned into heartbreak after a promotion sequence was ruled incomplete and illegal in a dramatic GCL encounter. With seconds left, Mishra’s dropped rook cost him crucial time, forcing him to replay the promotion with just one second remaining. He flagged instantly, handing Ganges Grandmasters a match-winning victory despite Mendonca’s apology.

title: From trains to stardom: Blind singer Suneel Lodhi's journey to Hanuman Ansh
content: Suneel Lodhi, a visually impaired folk singer from Bundelkhand, captured the nation's heart with his mesmerizing voice. For years, he enchanted audiences with bhajans and folk songs on village streets and local trains. His performance of "Maine Tere Hi Bharose" skyrocketed to fame after appearing in the film Hanuman Ansh, propelling him into a broader audience. His journey underscores the themes of unwavering faith and resilience before attaining fame.

title: Uber's layoff memo also has a work from home message for remaining 29,000 employees
content: Uber is cutting about 3,300 jobs, roughly 10% of its workforce, but chief executive Dara Khosrowshahi's email to staff carries a second decision for everyone who stays. Uber is ending work from home for all but 1% of employees, asking remote staff to move to an office near their team. The three-day hybrid policy stays, and Uber will enforce it, with global teams concentrated in New York and San Francisco.

title: Saharanpur mosque row: YouTuber Huda Zariwala held over remarks against CM Yogi
content: YouTuber Huda Zariwala was arrested in Saharanpur for allegedly making objectionable remarks. These remarks were reportedly made against the chief minister and district magistrate. The arrest occurred after she participated in a protest against a mosque demolition. The mosque was removed from the collectorate premises following a court order. Police are currently taking further legal action in this ongoing matter.

title: Watch: 15-year-old Sooryavanshi plots two big wickets in Duleep Trophy final
content: In the Duleep Trophy final, young talent Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, only 15, demonstrated remarkable tactical skills that greatly benefitted the East Zone team. He was instrumental in achieving two important dismissals and showcased his sharp decision-making through successful DRS calls. Furthermore, he cleverly recalled Mohammed Shami for a critical spell just before the tea break, solidifying his growing reputation in senior cricket.

title: How Apple iPhone Ultra could become the most expensive iPhone ever launched
content: Apple's Surprise and Shine event on September 9 is expected to bring the iPhone Ultra, the company's first foldable iPhone. IDC puts its average selling price above $2,550, or roughly Rs 2.25 lakh, with top storage variants crossing $3,000. Here is what the iPhone Ultra price, specs, 7.8-inch folding display and supply constraints look like ahead of launch, and why the memory shortage is pushing every iPhone 18 price higher.

title: Making example out of Aakriti, official excesses will make UP a dystopia: HC
content: In a pivotal ruling, the Allahabad High Court overturned the NSA detention of Akriti Chaudhary and granted her compensation. The judges faulted the Gautam Budh Nagar administration for presenting insufficient evidence and emphasized the need for bureaucrats to prioritize constitutional obligations over political affiliations. The absence of evidence indicating that Chaudhary incited violence signals a critical caution against the abuse of preventive detention laws aimed at activists.

title: Penguins in Chile are wearing copper vests to help them heal faster
content: In an inspiring initiative, Chilean researchers are designing specialized vests for injured penguins, incorporating copper and zinc to expedite healing. This groundbreaking effort is focused on supporting the struggling Humboldt penguin population by preventing further injury while enhancing recovery. The vests draw on effective treatments that have proven successful for domestic animals, showcasing a creative blend of technology and compassion.

title: 80-acre California town that drew 250 eBay bids is going up for sale again
content: Bridgeville, an 80-acre town in Northern California, made history in 2002 as the first town to be listed on eBay. The auction drew 250 bids, with the highest reaching $1.77 million, but the winner backed out. After several owners and failed plans, the town is set to return to the market this September, with its current owners hoping for someone who can help the community flourish.

title: How WhatsApp messages led to former USCIS official in $960,000 citizenship scam
content: A former USCIS official and an accomplice face federal charges for a bribery scheme. They allegedly accepted nearly $960,000 to manipulate immigration applications. Investigators used thousands of WhatsApp messages and calls to trace the alleged scam. The scheme involved bypassing standard procedures and speeding up citizenship cases. This alleged operation spanned over six years, from late 2019 to early 2026.

title: Sri M's journey from Kerala boy to Himalayan seeker and spiritual teacher
content: Sri M's path of spirituality started in his early years, leading him to seek wisdom in the Himalayas. He founded the Satsang Foundation with the mission of enhancing education for tribal children. His Walk of Hope was a remarkable initiative aimed at fostering interfaith unity throughout India. His autobiography and the esteemed Padma Bhushan award signal his profound impact, while he champions the profound benefits of walking and experiential learning.

title: Noida student served Rs 5 lakh peace-bond notice over Jantar Mantar protest
content: A Gautam Buddha University student received a peace bond notice after a protest. The student denied allegations and stated participation was peaceful. Authorities later revoked the notice after the matter came to attention. Police had alleged the student spread anti-government narratives on campus. The incident occurred amid legal proceedings for maintaining public order.

title: PM Modi holds four-hour review meeting with 20 ministers on governance, welfare
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi held a four-hour review meeting with ministers.  He focused on key government initiatives and their implementation on the ground.  Ministers presented progress reports on their respective departmental work.  Actionable ideas were sought for a developed India vision by 2047.  PM Modi stressed digital engagement and plans more such sessions.

title: Patrick Mahomes owns 3 sports teams: How did he build his Kansas City empire?
content: Patrick Mahomes has expanded his influence beyond the Kansas City Chiefs by becoming a part-owner of three professional sports franchises. His reported $10 million investment in the Kansas City Royals marked his entry into sports ownership. He later added stakes in Sporting Kansas City and the Kansas City Current alongside his wife, Brittany. While Mahomes continues pursuing NFL success, his growing investments are shaping a lasting business legacy in Kansas City.

title: Ayesha Curry on Stephen Curry’s Warriors season: What surprises did she predict?
content: Stephen Curry is entering his 18th Warriors season fresh off an injury-hit 2025-26 campaign that limited him to 43 games. His wife, Ayesha, says he's trained non-stop since the season ended and predicts surprises ahead. Curry, now eligible for a max extension under the NBA's Over-38 Rule, insists he wants to finish his career in Golden State and isn't letting contract talk distract from his preparation for the new season.

title: Shubman Gill turns 27: 10 records that chart his rise from prodigy to India captain
content: On his 27th birthday, Shubman Gill reflects on a remarkable cricketing journey filled with extraordinary accomplishments. As the fastest Indian to reach 1,000, 2,000, and 3,000 ODI runs, he continues to break barriers. Additionally, Gill is celebrated for his record as the youngest double-century scorer in ODIs and achieving the highest IPL playoff score.

title: Indian startup unveils testing & manufacturing hubs to validate reusable rocket stages
content: Indian space startup Agnikul Cosmos inaugurated two new facilities in Chennai. These facilities will support testing and manufacturing of reusable rocket stages. The company aims to develop reusable launch vehicle technology for future missions. Agnikul Cosmos already designs and manufactures its own rocket engines. This expansion marks a significant step in India's space program capabilities.

title: 2010 spot-fixing: When Amir, Butt and Asif brought shame to Pakistan cricket
content: The scandal took place during Pakistan's tour of England, during the fourth Test at Lord's. It centred on allegations that Pakistani players had deliberately bowled no-balls at specific points in the match in return for money.

title: Soha Ali Khan on why parents should not give children everything they want
content: Soha Ali Khan discusses her strategy for inspiring her daughter Inaaya to embrace reading. She acknowledges that at times, persuasion and incentives can play a vital role in sparking a child's interest. Khan underscores the importance of parental role modeling, noting that children often emulate the reading habits of their caregivers. By cultivating a visible reading environment, she believes parents can effectively nurture a love for books.

title: Realty’s next phase: Developers shift focus from debt cuts to new projects
content: In a notable shift, developers are prioritizing new project investments over merely mending their balance sheets. Although sales volumes have recently dipped, operating cash flow remains robust. The moderation in free cash flow reflects increased expenditures on land and assets. With much of the balance sheet refurbishment behind them and reduced leverage, this transformation signals strong developer confidence in the ongoing housing cycle and its anticipated growth.

title: Why Harry and Meghan were caught off guard by King Charles’ latest letter
content: King Charles III has clarified Prince Harry and Meghan's status as private citizens.  The royal family confirmed they remain non-working members, which was previously agreed.  This clarification came shortly before a letter was sent to senior officials.  Harry and Meghan continue their commercial and charitable work in their private capacity.  Their security arrangements remain a separate and ongoing discussion.

title: Worried about theft, Bihar family parks new SUV on rooftop with crane
content: A Bihar family placed their new SUV on their house rooftop for security.  The vehicle was lifted by a crane and positioned on the two-storied structure.  This unusual parking choice has sparked widespread discussion and varied public reactions.  Concerns have been raised regarding the building's structural capacity to bear the vehicle's weight.  The family sought a secure location after their driver departed for other opportunities.

title: Deepti Sharma moves up to 6th position; Sree Charani retains T20I no. 1 ranking
content: Sree Charani continues her dominance at the top of the Women's T20I bowling rankings. Following an impressive performance in the Asia Cup, Deepti Sharma has risen to sixth place. Noteworthy advancements were also observed for several other players in the rankings. Charlie Dean showed significant progress in both the ODI all-rounders and bowling categories, while Amy Hunter stood out as a top performer among ODI batters.

title: Cops make 6 apologise publicly for snatching Muslim man’s skull cap, file FIR suo motu
content: Six men were arrested after an incident during a procession in Marhera, Etah.  Video footage showed an elderly man's skullcap being snatched and thrown down.  Police registered an FIR invoking provisions related to communal harmony and rioting.  The arrested individuals were later made to publicly apologize for their actions.  This police action was widely praised for deterring similar disruptions to communal harmony.

title: India rolls out 400th Apache fuselage as defence sector takes off
content: Tata Boeing Aerospace has produced its 400th Apache helicopter fuselage in India. This achievement signifies India's growing defense manufacturing capabilities and global supply role. Indigenous defense production has significantly increased, with exports also showing dramatic growth. The government aims for substantial defense export targets by 2029. India's defense industrial base now includes numerous manufacturers and MSMEs across states.

title: 'I was disrespected': Ex-Pak coach names 'untouchable' figure behind England mess

title: Manipuri musician killed in Delhi was cousin of BAFTA-winning ‘Boong’ director
content: Chongtham Vikram Singh, a 55-year-old Manipuri musician, died after being beaten outside his Delhi home. He had gone downstairs to object to a group of men creating a disturbance. His family found him in a semi-conscious state and he was rushed to the hospital. Doctors found his condition too critical for surgery and he passed away. Manipuri associations and student groups are protesting and demanding justice for the musician.

title: 'Will also kill her sugar daddy': Guwahati man who beheaded wife, kept head in fridge
content: A Guwahati woman was allegedly killed by her husband after a quarrel.  Her body was found decapitated in a flat, with her head in a bag.  The accused surrendered to police after the incident occurred on September third.  He confessed to the crime, stating frequent arguments led to the fatal act.  A court has sent the accused to police custody for seven days.

title: Jaipur fort murder: Guide dies after knife attack; locals protest
content: A tourist guide died after a dispute over jeep access near Amer Fort.  Local residents protested and shut shops following the guide's death.  The argument reportedly escalated into a violent knife attack by two men.  Police detained the jeep driver and his associate after the incident.  The injured guide succumbed to his wounds while undergoing treatment.

title: Kangana supports Trisha amid her character assassination for link-up rumours with Vijay

She emphasized that such behavior is a global issue. Meanwhile, Udhayanidhi Stalin is facing legal repercussions over his comments in Tamil Nadu, prompting renewed conversations about the treatment of women in the public eye.

title: Woman divorced after father's death can get his family pension, Tripura HC rules
content: The Tripura high court ordered the Agartala Municipal Corporation to grant family pension benefits.  A divorced daughter was eligible for the pension from her divorce date.  The court found the corporation's rejection of the claim was incorrect.  Pension rules do not require divorce at the pensioner's death.  Arrears and interest were directed to be paid within three months.

title: 'Strong chargesheet in two weeks': Kiren Rijiju on Manipuri musician's murder in Delhi
content: All eight accused in the alleged killing of Chongtham Vikram Singh have been arrested. Police assured the family a strong chargesheet will be filed within two weeks. The musician died after an altercation with delivery boys and dhaba workers. His body will be taken to Manipur on Wednesday for final rites. Authorities hope for strict punishment for those responsible for the incident.

title: Shiva Rajkumar calls Hindi ‘national language’, sparks controversy
content: Kannada actor Shiva Rajkumar's recent comments about Hindi have ignited a significant social media debate. He referred to Hindi as a national language during his film's title launch event. Critics objected to this description, while supporters argued he meant widespread usage. The controversy surrounds his upcoming pan-India film 'Original Monster'. This incident highlights ongoing discussions about language and regional identity in cinema.

title: How China's exercise with Egypt made the IAF better suited to take on the dragon
content: Chinese J-16 fighters met Indian Rafale jets during an Egyptian air exercise.  The Rafale's advanced SPECTRA system logged Chinese radar signatures for future analysis.  This encounter provided India with crucial data for potential future air combat scenarios.  However, differences in weaponry and doctrine limit direct comparisons to Indian Rafales.  The exercise offered China limited insight into countering India's full Rafale capabilities.

title: SC rejects panel's plea for 6 more months to define Aravali hills & ranges
content:
NEW DELHI: "Why don't you simply say that the matter be heard after my retirement," asked an exasperated CJI Surya Kant as a bench led by him outrightly declined a request from the high-powered committee for six more months' time to draft a comprehensive definition of Aravali hills and ranges to protect the eco-sensitive area from mining and various commercial activities and fixed a Nov 30 deadline for submission of the final report. Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for HPC, told a bench of CJI, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that HPC would need six more months to file a detailed report, which would include completing public hearings and considering views of stakeholders. CJI Kant is to retire on Feb 9. A bench led by him had stayed the operation of SC's Nov 20 judgement accepting a very liberal definition of Aravali that had caused an uproar among environmentalists.

End of Article
